title: ephemeral-profiles-ttl-and-changelog-rollup-for-fast-experiments
author: Asha Menon
body:
Motivation: teams run short-lived experiments and create numerous temporary model profiles which clutter the registry and inflate changelog noise. This PR introduces an ephemeral profile TTL mechanism, an allowance for automated consolidation of ephemeral edits into a periodic changelog rollup, and a lightweight CLI + server-side lifecycle to manage expiration and rollup.

What this change does (high level):
- Adds a 'ttl_seconds' optional field to model profile metadata. Profiles marked ephemeral (ttl_seconds set) expire automatically and move into a 'staged-archive' bucket after TTL.
- Introduces a changelog-rollup job that consolidates ephemeral churn into a single weekly digest entry and appends a short summary to the canonical changelog.
- Adds mrctl commands: 'mrctl profile expire --id' and 'mrctl profile gc --dry-run' to preview and force-gc ephemeral profiles.
- Implements safeguards: a 24h grace period after TTL expiry (configurable), owner notification via audit-event, and an opt-out label (retain: true) to prevent accidental deletion.
- Backwards-compatible: profiles without ttl_seconds behave as before. Rollup only touches profiles with the ephemeral tag and configured TTL.

Key implementation notes:
- Server: packages/registry/src/ttl_manager.rs handles TTL scheduling and moves expired profiles to a compact archive store. A sidecar cron (scripts/ephemeral_gc_runner.py) runs the same workflow in Private installs where a background worker isn't available.
- Changelog rollup: scripts/changelog_rollup.py aggregates ephemeral profile diffs into one bulletized summary and produces a single changelog artifact every week. The server exposes /admin/rollup to preview rollups.
- CLI: cli/mrctl/src/commands/expire.rs (implements expire/gc/dry-run) and cli docs updated.
- Tests: added e2e test for TTL lifecycle and unit tests for diff-aggregation logic.

Migration and rollout plan:
1) Deploy server code behind feature flag 'ephemeral-ttl' (default off) and enable for internal staging.
2) Run caretaker job in staging to build a rollup dry-run for validation.
3) Turn on rollup in a throttled window (weekly) with monitoring for archive size and changelog growth.
4) After two successful weekly rollups, enable TTL enforcement.

Monitoring and safety:
- New metrics: registry.ephemeral.expire.count, registry.ephemeral.rollup.size_tokens, registry.ephemeral.archive.size_bytes.
- Alerts: high archive growth (P1), rollup failure rate > 5% (P2).
- Audit events emitted for every automatic archive and owner notification recorded.

Security & Compliance:
- Archive store is encrypted with the registry KMS key.
- Retention and access controls honored; archived profiles remain discoverable to admins and subject to existing data export workflows. Legal reviewed the opt-out and notification flows.

Checklist:
- [x] Server TTL manager + archive path
- [x] Changelog rollup job + preview endpoint
- [x] CLI expire/gc commands + docs
- [x] Unit and e2e tests
- [x] Metrics + alerts
- [x] Migration plan + feature flag

Follow-ups (post-merge):
- ENG-2120: Add UI controls for profile TTL and rollup preview in the Console.
- ENG-2139: Implement per-org rollup cadence (weekly/bi-weekly/monthly).

Notes: This design intentionally keeps ephemeral profiles reversible for 30 days post-archive to minimize accidental data loss. The rollup text retains links to archived profile IDs to assist debugging and audit.

review_comments:
Diego Alvarez: Please add more logs around what fields are preserved during archive — we need context for rollback.
Author (Asha): Added structured archive metadata including preserved_fields list and original_owner in ttl_manager.rs.
Maya Li: Rollup needs to cap the summary length — very long diffs will bloat the changelog UI.
Author (Asha): Implemented a 2k char summarizer and an artifact link to full diff in storage.
Samir Patel: Are we sure encryption keys are available in Private installer? Edge case of air-gapped installs.
Author (Asha): Added ephemeral_gc_runner.py to run locally against the customer's key material; documented in docs/ephemeral-profiles.md.
QA (Ravi): Found flaky timing in e2e where clock skew caused immediate expiry.
Author (Asha): Added clock tolerance window and test harness fix.
Review outcome: approvals from Diego and Maya after last changes; Samir requested final compliance doc which was added. CI passed on final run.
